task.title: Persist exact recurrence occurrence provenance through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/879 by exposing the kernel's revision-bound exact occurrence persistence as a bounded CLI command.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence identity before storage access and delegate revision, bounds, duplicate, and replay guarantees to the recurrence store.
Emit the established compact deterministic occurrence JSON after one successful append.
Keep persisted provenance inert and grant no due, claim, materialization, dispatch, retry, or execution authority.

attempts.summary: Established RED writable recurrence CLI coverage.
attempts.diagnostic: Focused CLI integration tests failed because recurrence persist was not a recognized subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added success, pre-open identity validation, missing, stale, out-of-range, duplicate, reopen, exact JSON, and first-write preservation tests.

attempts.diagnostic: Reimplementing projection or append validation in the CLI would duplicate the kernel's authoritative permission boundary.
attempts.patch: Added recurrence persist, delegated mutation to RecurrenceStore::persist_occurrence, reused occurrence serialization, categorized failures, and documented ADR-0046.

attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit initially returned a false-green rate-limited status instead of substantive review evidence.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled through the stated cooldown, deliberately resumed review, and merged only after the exact head had a no-actionable-comments review and successful Rust quality gate.

outcome.summary: The CLI now records one exact immutable recurrence occurrence with deterministic output while preserving the kernel-owned revision and execution-authority boundaries.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0172-recurrence-occurrence-persistence-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 174 records: 174 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: A writable CLI should adapt the kernel's mutation contract rather than reproduce authoritative projection or append checks.
Validate identity before opening storage so malformed input cannot create or mutate a database.
Duplicate persistence must preserve the first immutable occurrence record.
A green rate-limited review status is not review evidence; preserve merge state until substantive review capacity returns.
Persisted occurrence provenance remains evidence rather than execution authority.
